summary: The lecture covers the making of the Indian Constitution, tracing the evolution from divine right of kings to social contract theory, the demand for a Constituent Assembly (first by M.N. Roy), the Cabinet Mission Plan (1946) which structured the Assembly's composition (389 members: 296 elected indirectly from British provinces, 93 nominated from princely states), its functioning through 12 sessions, the Objective Resolution (moved by Nehru, became Preamble), the Drafting Committee chaired by Dr. B.R. Ambedkar, adoption on 26 November 1949 and enforcement on 26 January 1950, along with key criticisms.
points: Constituent Assembly demand first raised by M.N. Roy (radical democracy) in 1934; INC officially demanded in 1935; Nehru insisted on universal adult franchise in 1938.
Cabinet Mission Plan (May 1946) by Pethick-Lawrence, Cripps, A.V. Alexander; proposed 389 members: 296 British India (indirect election via provincial assemblies), 93 Princely States (nomination).
Elections held July-August 1946: Congress won 208 seats, Muslim League 73; Princely States' 93 seats initially unfilled; Assembly partly elected, partly nominated.
First meeting 9 December 1946; Dr. Sachidanand Sinha interim president; Dr. Rajendra Prasad elected president 11 December; H.C. Mukherjee vice-president.
Objective Resolution moved by Nehru 13 December 1946, unanimously adopted 22 January 1947; became Preamble of Constitution.
Indian Independence Act 1947 made Assembly sovereign and legislative body (Parliament); Dr. Rajendra Prasad chaired constitutional work, G.V. Mavalankar chaired legislative work.

Drafting Committee appointed 29 August 1947, chaired by Dr. B.R. Ambedkar; members: Gopalaswami Ayyangar, Alladi Krishnaswami Ayyar, K.M. Munshi, Syed Mohammad Saadullah, N. Madhava Rau, T.T. Krishnamachari.
Constitution adopted 26 November 1949 with 394 Articles, 8 Schedules; enacted 26 January 1950 with 395 Articles, 8 Schedules, 22 Parts; took 2 years 11 months 18 days; cost ₹6.4 million.

Criticisms: not truly representative (indirect election, limited franchise, nomination), not initially sovereign (Cabinet Mission basis), time-consuming, Congress dominance, lawyer-politician domination, Hindu dominance.
Proportional representation with single transferable vote used for Constituent Assembly elections; later adopted for Presidential elections in Constitution.

check.q: Who moved the Objective Resolution in the Constituent Assembly on 13 December 1946?
What was the total membership of the Constituent Assembly as per the Cabinet Mission Plan?
Which Act made the Constituent Assembly a sovereign body and also the legislative body (Parliament) of India?

title: Complete Indian Polity for UPSC CSE 2025-26 | Ch-2 |  Making of Indian Constitution | Shashank Tyagi
